content: Loracarbef is no longer available in the United States. If you are currently taking this medication, you should contact your doctor to discuss transitioning to an alternative treatment. Loracarbef is an antibiotic that is prescribed to treat bacterial infections, including pneumonia, bronchitis, and infections of the ear, nose, throat, skin, and urinary tract. It is important to note that antibiotics like loracarbef are ineffective against viral infections such as colds or the flu. If you have questions about other potential uses of this medication, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Loracarbef is available in capsule form or as a liquid suspension, both of which are taken orally. It is typically administered once daily or every 12 hours (twice daily) for a duration of 7 to 14 days. Follow the instructions on your prescription label precisely, and ask your doctor or pharmacist for clarification if needed. Do not take more or less of the medication than prescribed, and do not take it more frequently than directed. Swallow the capsules whole with a full glass of water. Even if you start feeling better, continue taking loracarbef for the full prescribed duration unless instructed otherwise by your doctor. Before starting loracarbef, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to loracarbef, cephalosporin antibiotics (e.g., cefadroxil or cephalexin), penicillin, or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially other antibiotics, anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), probenecid, or vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of kidney or liver disease, colitis, or gastrointestinal issues. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Should you become pregnant while taking loracarbef, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking loracarbef. Take loracarbef on an empty stomach, either at least one hour before a meal or two hours after eating. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Loracarbef may cause side effects. Minor side effects include upset stomach, diarrhea, vomiting, and mild skin rash. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Severe side effects require immediate medical attention and include severe skin rash, itching, hives, difficulty breathing or swallowing, wheezing, and vaginal infections. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store loracarbef in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not freeze the medication. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as certain tests may be required to monitor your response to loracarbef. If you have diabetes, consult your doctor before making any changes to your diet or medication regimen. Use Clinistix or TesTape to test your urine for sugar while taking loracarbef, as Clinitest is not recommended. Do not share this medication with others, and note that your prescription is likely not refillable. If your symptoms persist after completing the course of loracarbef, contact your doctor. Loracarbef is marketed under the brand names Lorabid® and Lorabid® Pulvules®.
